newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA Healthcare profits rise in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA Healthcare profits rise in first quarter.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp., which has agreed to acquire Value Health Inc. for about $1.2 billion, said first-quarter profits grew as it strengthened its position as the nation's largest health care services provider.
Net income grew to $479 million in the quarter from $416 million in the year-ago period. Earnings per share rose to 70 cents from 61 cents, matching analysts' consensus estimates.
Revenues rose to $5.3 billion from $5.0 billion.

"We believe that Columbia's success is the result of our continued focus on measuring and improving clinical outcomes, measuring and improving patient satisfaction, measuring and improving costs and providing service with compassion," said Chairman Richard Scott.

Columbia/HCA said outpatient revenues accounted for 38 percent of total patient revenues, up from 36 percent in the 1996 quarter, due to growth in homecare services, outpatient surgery and other ancillary services.
Columbia's home care agencies provided about 4.2 million home care visits during the first quarter, up from about 3 million visits in the 1996 period, it said.
Surgery cases at company hospitals and ambulatory surgery centres rose 5 percent on a same-facility basis.
On April 14, Columbia agreed to pay $20.50 in cash for each Value Health common share, instead of acquiring the speciality health care services company in a tax-free stock swap announced in January.
Columbia operates 342 hospitals, 148 outpatient surgery centres, more than 570 home care locations and extensive ancillary services in 36 states, England, Switzerland and Spain.
Columbia's stock rose 87.5 cents to $35.25 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
